messages:
jess: Hey team — PR #19999 is ready for merge with the new embedding-cache eviction heuristics. This touches runtime cache logic and autoscaler hints. Need runtime + infra + security eyes before I merge. @mike @sam @olga can you take a look? Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/19999 :eyes:

mike: I can own infra perf verification. I'll run the small-scale perf suite and the cluster eviction sim. ETA ~45m.

sam: Skimming now. Main concern is the fallback path when KV misses and the batcher behavior at 1k qps. If we can prove no latency spike, i'm fine.

olga: Security quick check: does this change surface any user-provided inputs to cache keys? If yes, we need to validate and add a test.

jess: good q — no user inputs are hashed into keys, only model+prompt-prefix+seqlen. I added a unit test that verifies deterministic keying.

priya: running load test against the PR branch. Running: `./scripts/loadtest --concurrency 200 --duration 10m --branch pr/19999` Will post numbers.

sam: if priya's numbers look stable, I can sign off for runtime. Also adding a note: watch for increased mem usage after warmup.

mike: infra perf run done: no significant tail latency change in the eviction sim. Peak mem bump +6% during warmup, settles to +1%. I captured logs: ```
# summary
p50: 12ms
p95: 48ms
p99: 120ms
mem_delta_warmup: +6%
mem_delta_steady: +1%
```

olga: thanks. I reviewed the inputs + test; no user-data leakage risk. Two small asks: 1) add a comment explaining why the constant TTL was removed, 2) add a changelog note for audit. Otherwise ok from security. :thumbsup:

jess: noted — will push a tiny follow-up commit for the comment + changelog.

canary-bot: Canary scheduled for PR 19999 on staging at 2026-03-18T02:30:00Z. Watch the canary-channel for alerts.

sam: With mike's perf numbers and olga's signoff, i'm happy to approve runtime. +1 from me.

mike: +1 infra.

olga: +1 sec.

jess: awesome — merging in 10m unless anyone objects. Thanks all. :rocket:
